# PowerPoint-authored sample decks

Committed binaries, and the only ones in this repository. Everything else
under `tests/fixtures/` is generated by `build_decks.py` and gitignored.

## Why these exist

Every other deck in the suite was built by python-pptx, which is a real limit
on what the suite can prove. python-pptx cannot author SmartArt at all, and
nothing it produces has sections, transitions, or animations. A library can
pass a test suite built entirely from its own output and still be wrong about
the format.

They paid for themselves on the first run. `smartart.pptx` exposed two defects
that every generated fixture had hidden:

1. **The integrity harness rejected valid PowerPoint output.**
   `dsp:dataModelExt/@relId` resolves against the relationships of the part
   that *refers* to the diagram data part, not the data part's own — which has
   none at all. The harness checked it against the containing part and
   reported every PowerPoint-authored diagram as damaged.
2. **`duplicate_slide` silently produced a wrong deck.** python-pptx has no
   model class for a diagram data part, so it loads as an opaque blob with no
   element tree, and the relationship-id rewrite skipped it entirely. The copy
   kept the original's `relId`, so its diagram pointed at the *original's*
   drawing cache. No exception and no repair prompt: PowerPoint recomputes the
   drawing on open and looks correct, while every other renderer draws the
   wrong thing or nothing.

Both are now covered by `tests/test_pptx_samples.py`. Neither was reachable
from a generated deck.

## Provenance

| | |
|---|---|
| Authored | 2026-08-14 |
| PowerPoint | Microsoft 365, `C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16` |
| OS | Windows 11 Home 26200 |
| Method | Scripted through [`pptlive`](https://github.com/thomas-villani/pptlive), driving a live PowerPoint instance over COM |

Scripted rather than clicked, so the decks are reproducible and the steps are
recorded rather than remembered. The commands are below; each was run against
a running PowerPoint with the deck open.

### `smartart.pptx`

One slide, one SmartArt process diagram. The highest-value binary here: it is
the only source anywhere in the suite of all five diagram parts and of the
unqualified `relId`.

```bash
# starting from a blank one-slide deck
pptlive shape add --slide 1 --kind smartart --smartart-kind process \
    --nodes '["Discover","Design","Build","Ship"]' \
    --left 60 --top 170 --width 600 --height 260
pptlive save-as tests/fixtures/pptx_samples/smartart.pptx --overwrite
```

Contains `/ppt/diagrams/{data,layout,colors,quickStyle,drawing}1.xml`. The
`drawing` part is reached by a Microsoft-extension relationship type that
python-pptx does not define — see `RT_DIAGRAM_DRAWING`.

### `real_world.pptx`

Three slides carrying the things python-pptx cannot author: PowerPoint's own
sections, a transition, an entrance animation, speaker notes, and a slide-jump
hyperlink. Built on top of the SmartArt deck.

```bash
pptlive write --anchor-id ph:1:title --text "Process"
pptlive slide add --layout title_and_content
pptlive write --anchor-id ph:2:title --text "Numbers"
pptlive shape add --slide 2 --kind chart --chart-type column \
    --categories 'Q1,Q2,Q3' --series '{"Revenue":[10,20,30]}' \
    --left 60 --top 150 --width 700 --height 330
pptlive slide add --layout title_only
pptlive write --anchor-id ph:3:title --text "Notes and links"
pptlive shape add --slide 3 --kind textbox --text "Back to the process" \
    --left 60 --top 200 --width 400 --height 50
pptlive shape set-link --anchor-id shape:3:2 --slide 1
pptlive write --anchor-id notes:3 --text "Speaker notes authored in PowerPoint."
pptlive slide set-transition --slide 2 --effect fade --duration 0.5
pptlive shape animate --anchor-id ph:2:title --effect fade
pptlive section add --name "Overview"
pptlive section add --name "Detail" --before-slide 2
pptlive save-as tests/fixtures/pptx_samples/real_world.pptx --overwrite
```

## Still missing

Neither of these blocks v0.1, but both would strengthen the suite:

- **Embedded video.** `pptlive` has no verb for inserting media, so this needs
  a manual Insert > Video. The case that matters is
  `get_or_add_video_media_part`, which mints an `RT.MEDIA` *and* an `RT.VIDEO`
  relationship to a single part — two relationship ids, one target, which is
  precisely the collapse the relationship map must tolerate. Covered
  synthetically today by `test_a_many_to_one_map_is_accepted`.
- **A custom show.** `pptlive` has no verb for one either. Covered by a
  hand-built `custom_show` fixture in `build_decks.py`, whose shape is a
  reasonable approximation but has never been checked against PowerPoint's.

## Regenerating

Don't, unless a test needs something new. These are inputs, not outputs: a
regenerated deck differs in timestamps, revision ids and part ordering, which
makes the diff unreadable and proves nothing. If you do regenerate, re-run
`uv run pytest tests/test_pptx_samples.py` and update the table above.

## Manual acceptance

Automated checks cannot answer "does PowerPoint open this without complaint."
Once per release, for each sample:

1. Duplicate slide 0 with `duplicate_slide`, save, and open in PowerPoint.
2. Confirm **no repair prompt**, and that the copy renders identically
   (`pptlive snapshot` makes this checkable rather than a matter of memory).
3. Save from PowerPoint, reopen with the library, and re-run the battery.
4. Duplicate again from PowerPoint's own output and re-run it once more —
   PowerPoint's serializer is not python-pptx's, and the library has to accept
   both.

Last run **2026-08-14**, against `smartart.pptx`, on the commit that added
these files. All four steps passed: no repair prompt, the two slides rendered
identically, and PowerPoint's re-save kept the diagrams as two independent
five-part sets — which is the real confirmation that the copy was genuinely
independent rather than an alias PowerPoint would have collapsed.
